 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE VIBHU BAKHRU  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SACHIN DATTA  ORDER % 09.09.2024 1.
The petitioners claim that they are the land owners in respect of the lands located in Khasra Nos.61 min, situated in the Revenue Estate of Village Behlolpur Khadar, Tehsil Mehrauli, NCT of Delhi.

2. The petitioner in W.P.(C) 6122/2015 claims ownership of land admeasuring 1 Bigha 10 Biswas,
while the petitioners in W.P.(C) 6133/2015 and W.P.(C) 6142/2015 claim ownership of land admeasuring 10 Biswas each.
3.

The petitioners have challenged Notification No. F.9(1)/89/L&B, issued on 23.06.1989 under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereafter Act of 1894), inter-alia, for acquisition of the subject lands.

The said notification was followed by Notification No.F.9(1)-L&B (ii) & (iii), dated 22.06.1990, issued under Section 6 and Section 17(1) of the Act of 1894, and the award No.15/92-93,
issued on 19.06.1992.
4.
It is the case of the petitioners that no compensation was paid in respect of the acquisition of the subject lands and the possession of the same was also not taken over.

The petitioners, accordingly,
claimed that by virtue of Section 24 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Re-Settlement Act, 2013 (hereafter Act of This is a digitally signed order.

sentences.text: The Delhi Development Authority had filed a Special Leave Petition (SLP) seeking leave to appeal the said decision before the Supreme Court.
The said leave was granted and the SLP was converted in Civil Appeal No.- 7409/2022 captioned Delhi Development Authority V. Saad Firoz & Ors.
7. By order dated 17.10.2022, the said appeal was allowed on the ground that this Court had not examined that the possession of the subject lands had been taken over.

It is material to note that in the meanwhile, the Supreme Court had delivered a judgement in Indore Development Authority V.
Manoharlal & Ors.: (2020) 8 SCC 129, authoritatively holding that for acquisition to lapse by virtue of Section 24 (2) of the 2013 Act, both the conditions - possession of the subject lands had not been taken over and compensation had not been paid - were required to be cumulatively satisfied.

sentences.text: 8. These petitions were accordingly remanded to this court to, inter alia, consider the question whether the possession of the subject lands were taken over by the LAC (respondent nos. 4 and 5).

9. The LAC has filed an affidavit in W.P.(C) 6122/2015, inter alia, affirming as under:
'7.
That it is submitted that possession of the Khasra No.61(17-01) This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 21/09/2024 at 04:20:30 was taken over and handed over to the beneficiary department on 27.12.1990 and 21.04.2006.

However, as per Statement 'A'
compensation has not been paid to the recorded owner.

Copies of possession proceedings dated 27.12.1990 and 21.04.2006 with true translation and typed copies are annexed herewith and marked as Annexure -R4/2 (Colly)'
10.
The LAC have also annexed along with that affidavit, proceedings whereby the possession of the subject lands were taken over.
11. In view of the above, the relief as sought by the petitioners cannot be granted.
12. The acquisition of the subject lands, under Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act has not lapsed as the LAC had taken over possession of the subject lands.
Consequently, both the conditions under Section 24(2) are not cumulatively satisfied.

13. At this stage, learned counsel for the petitioner requests that since, admittedly, the petitioners have not received compensation for the past several years; the respondents be directed to immediately disburse the same.
14. In the facts and circumstances of this case, we consider it apposite to direct the respondents to take expeditious steps for disbursal of the compensation, in accordance with law.
15. The petitions are dismissed with the aforesaid observations.
